# Contributing

<!-- Generated by scrum-github (preset standard). Edit it freely: init never overwrites it. -->

## Branches

| Branch | What it holds | Who writes to it |
|---|---|---|
| `{{RELEASE_BRANCH}}` | Released code. Every version tag (`{{TAG_PREFIX}}1.2.0`) is on this branch. | Release and hotfix pull requests only |
| `{{WORKING_BRANCH}}` | Work that is done but not released yet. | Pull requests from task branches |
| `feat/<task>-<slug>`, `fix/...` | One task. Created from `{{WORKING_BRANCH}}`. | You |
| `hotfix/<task>-<slug>` | An urgent fix of a released version. Created from `{{RELEASE_BRANCH}}`. | You |

Code moves one way: task branch → `{{WORKING_BRANCH}}` → `{{RELEASE_BRANCH}}`. Only `hotfix/*` starts
from `{{RELEASE_BRANCH}}`. Nobody pushes to `{{WORKING_BRANCH}}` or `{{RELEASE_BRANCH}}` directly: every change goes
through a pull request, which needs the required checks and the review.

## Pull requests

- Target `{{WORKING_BRANCH}}`. A pull request from a task branch into `{{RELEASE_BRANCH}}` fails the
  source-branch check; only `release/*` and `hotfix/*` may target `{{RELEASE_BRANCH}}`.
- The title follows [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org): a type (`feat`,
  `fix`, `docs`, `chore`, `refactor`, `test`, `ci`, `perf`, `build`, `revert`), an optional scope,
  `!` for a breaking change, then `: ` and a summary. Example: `feat(auth): log in with email`.
- The description closes its task: `Closes #<task number>`. A change without a task gets the
  `{{NO_TASK_LABEL}}` label instead.
- Squash-merge task pull requests into `{{WORKING_BRANCH}}`. A back-merge (`{{RELEASE_BRANCH}}` → `{{WORKING_BRANCH}}`) is
  merged with a merge commit, never squashed.

A task merged into `{{WORKING_BRANCH}}` stays In review with the label `{{LOCATION_PREFIX}}{{WORKING_BRANCH}}`; it is Done when
its code reaches `{{RELEASE_BRANCH}}` in a release.

## Releases

1. `/scrum-github:release` opens a release pull request from `release/<tag>` into `{{RELEASE_BRANCH}}`
   with the version, the release notes and the updated version files.
2. Review it and merge it with a merge commit. The release workflow then creates the tag and the
   GitHub Release, sets the released tasks Done and opens the back-merge into `{{WORKING_BRANCH}}`.
3. Merge the back-merge pull request with a merge commit.

A hotfix: `/scrum-github:hotfix <task>` creates `hotfix/<task>-<slug>` from `{{RELEASE_BRANCH}}`; its pull request
targets `{{RELEASE_BRANCH}}` and publishes a patch version when merged.
